defects.description: The half-open overlap test uses `<=` on both sides, so two intervals that merely touch at an endpoint (e.g. [0,5) and [5,9)) are reported as overlapping even though they share no interior point.
defects.anchor: return a[0] <= b[1] and b[0] <= a[1]
paraphrases: Comparing endpoints with less-than-or-equal treats an interval's exclusive end as inclusive, so adjacent ranges meeting at a single boundary are wrongly judged to intersect.
The overlap predicate admits equality at the shared edge, causing back-to-back half-open intervals that only abut to be classified as overlapping.
Because the boundary is included on both comparisons, ranges that touch without any common point are counted as overlapping contrary to the half-open convention.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '    return a[0] < b[1] and b[0] < a[1]'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The overlap's lower bound is taken as the smaller of the two starts instead of the larger, so `overlap_amount` computes an inflated width and even returns a positive amount for disjoint intervals.
defects.anchor: lo = a[0] if a[0] < b[0] else b[0]
paraphrases: The intersection's left edge should be the later of the two starts, but the code picks the earlier one, overstating the shared length and yielding a nonzero result for ranges that do not meet.
Choosing the minimum start rather than the maximum makes the computed overlap span reach further left than the true intersection, breaking the disjoint-returns-zero contract.
Because `lo` binds to whichever start is smaller, the overlap measure is too large and can report coverage between intervals that actually have none in common.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '    lo = a[0] if a[0] > b[0] else b[0]'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: Merging combines runs only when the next start is strictly less than the previous end, so intervals that touch (`start == last_end`) are left separate instead of fusing, contradicting the documented merge-on-touch behavior.
paraphrases: Using strict less-than as the coalesce test excludes the exact-adjacency case, so abutting intervals like [0,5) and [5,9) are not joined into one.
The merge condition drops equality, meaning a following interval that begins right where the current one ends is emitted as a distinct range rather than merged.
Because touching endpoints no longer satisfy the combine check, adjacent intervals that should collapse into a single span stay split apart.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        if start <= last_end:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: Activity selection accepts an interval only when its start is strictly greater than the last chosen end, so a candidate beginning exactly at that end (which is non-overlapping under the half-open rule) is wrongly rejected, shrinking the selected set.
defects.anchor: if current_end is None or start > current_end:
paraphrases: The greedy acceptance uses strict greater-than, excluding an interval that starts precisely where the previous selection finished even though the two do not overlap.
Because equality with the running end is disallowed, a valid non-conflicting activity whose start meets the last end is skipped, producing a smaller-than-maximal subset.
The selection gate demands the next start be past the current end rather than at-or-past it, so back-to-back half-open intervals cannot both be chosen.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        if current_end is None or start >= current_end:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.
